title: Tencent raises $5.7bn in bonds as AI investment soars
source_used: Business Day (South Africa), read in full; the text carries no wire credit
key_facts: Tencent raised about $5.7 billion on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026: $1.3 billion of 10-year and $500 million of 20-year dollar bonds, 20 billion yuan of 10-year and 6 billion yuan of 30-year offshore yuan bonds.
Combined orders exceeded $23 billion, more than four times the final offering size; Tencent had been expected to raise at least $4.5 billion.
Proceeds are for general corporate purposes, per the term sheet, as Tencent increases investment in AI infrastructure and products.
The dollar bonds priced at 90 and 115 basis points over US Treasuries, 25 points tighter than initial guidance; the 10-year yuan bonds priced at 2.40% and the 30-year at 3.00%.

Tencent's capital expenditure more than doubled to 96.3 billion yuan in the first half of 2026 from 45.9 billion yuan a year earlier; it last tapped the bond market in June, raising about $4.66 billion.
Tencent shares fell 0.1% on Tuesday and are down about 29% this year; the bonds are expected to be rated A1 by Moody's and A+ by S&P.
Gary Tan of Allspring Global Investments said the quick return suggests capital remains available for AI for companies with strong cash flows, balance sheets and credible monetisation plans.
quote_evidence: Tencent Holdings raised about $5.7bn through dollar and offshore yuan debt offerings on Tuesday, drawing combined investor orders of more than $23bn even as AI spending jitters hit global markets.
Tencent's capital expenditure more than doubled to 96.3-billion yuan in the first half of 2026 from 45.9-billion yuan a year earlier, according to its offering documents.

Its return to the bond market so quickly suggests capital remains available for AI, particularly for companies with strong cash flows, balance sheets and credible monetisation plans, said Allspring Global Investments portfolio manager Gary Tan.
why_it_matters_hint: A large, oversubscribed bond sale shows capital is still available for AI spenders with strong finances.
notes: Follow-up of the 12 Oct 2026 edition (Bloomberg: Tencent told investors its $5 billion bond was mainly for AI spending; planned sale could price as early as Tuesday). The Business Day text names no wire service and may be a wire story; Reuters' analysis (C07-01) confirms the Tuesday sale and the 1.15-point guidance over Treasuries.
